P1.evidence: Setter notes genuinely read back — 'I know you spoke with Kim. He kind of gave me a little bit of a head start, said, you're working with a trainer, but not too engaged, looking out the window, which isn't great.' Frame ran three-part: 'I just want to get a better idea of things, build out what it is that you want. If we can help, we'll talk about it. If not, that's fine too' — no 'what's in the way' or 'what you need'. Agreement sought only as 'All right.' Open question ran and he handled her attempt to redirect well: 'let's start with what were you hoping we could potentially help with, and then we can ask each other some questions.'

P2.evidence: Weight and height both asked directly ('how much do you weigh right now?', 'how tall are you'); age never asked and only inferable from 'you're over 50'. Occupation never asked at all, which is the single ICP criterion that matters commercially. Injuries handled properly — he asked, she deflected ('I mean, I think it's fine'), and he rephrased: 'Let me rephrase the question. Any restrictions, would you say...' which surfaced the back. Training week fully mapped ('How many days a week do you train normally?' → weights x3, runs x2, stretch, rest). Food asked twice and specifically ('What kind of stuff do you eat, though, when you go out?'). Results from current training established indirectly through the trainer complaint and the 120→150 timeline, not asked as a question. No health conditions or hereditary question, no sleep, no energy.

P3.evidence: Surface goals captured and confirmed back ('So thigh gap, lose 25 pounds, back fat, belly fat, gone') but never developed. No 'one thing you'd change', no mobility/strength/energy question, no 'something physical you can't do right now' — she volunteered exactly that ('I can't do that stretch that he's doing') and it went unused. The whole deep half of the phase is absent: no bridge to what is actually driving it, no 'what does that do for you', no 'who else does that impact' despite the husband literally walking into the room mid-call and wanting the same change, and no reflect-back. For a prospect whose stated goals are entirely cosmetic, this is the phase that would have built the price.

P4.evidence: Asked about the current provider rather than past attempts — 'your trainer, what's he doing that you don't like so that we don't replicate anything?' — which was a strong question and produced the disengagement complaint. Outcome named, but by the rep: 'Unfortunately, you didn't get the result and that's just life.' The bottleneck was also diagnosed by the rep rather than by her — 'some work to do on the nutrition, for sure. Sounds like... That's your biggest bottleneck' — though she then owned it ('it's the kitchen that gets me, and I think the kitchen is probably 80%'). Never asked why it did not stick, and never ran 'the information isn't the problem — why can't you stick to it on your own?', which was the obvious question for someone who trains six days a week and drinks a cocktail and two glasses of wine every night.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame. The two-year question was never asked of a woman who had just described a four-to-five-year, thirty-pound drift with no natural stopping point. 'Draw a line in the sand' appeared only as a rapport reflection about the couple — 'You both are like, let's draw a line in the sand with this moment kind of thing' — not as the scripted ask, and nothing was built on it.

P6.evidence: Neither commitment question was asked. The rep substituted a clarity-scale check before pricing — 'if were to put it on a 10, where are you at in terms of the process? Is anything you feel like is missing?' — which tested comprehension, not commitment, and got 'I think it's great. It makes sense. It's understandable. It's logical.' He moved to numbers on that, without ever asking whether she believed she could get there or whether anything would stop her going all in.

P11.evidence: The call reached the point where payment should have been asked for — price was presented, every question was answered, she said 'this sounds good' and 'I feel very well-informed to be able to make the decision' — and no ask was made. No payment, no onboarding call booked, no agreement sent, no welcome email, Skool link or questionnaire mentioned. The rep even supplied the mechanism that removes the timing blocker ('we still get you onboarded anyway... the first day of your six months is your first day that you train') and then did not use it to close, ending on 'Text me when you're ready.'

objection_plays.detail: Timing blocker was roughly six weeks of prepaid Equinox sessions. The rep improvised a genuinely good structural answer — onboard now, start the clock on the first training day — and separately handled the summer-travel version with a pause policy. But none of the scripted OD moves ran: no 'things never slow down', no 'the only thing you can control is right now', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started'. Having removed the obstacle, he did not convert it into a decision.

She ended on 'what do I do when I'm like, okay, Harry, I'm ready. Like sign me up' followed by an errand list. The rep answered 'Super simple. We'd just book in another call' and helped her plan the exit conversation with her trainer. No 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you there', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no isolation of what is actually preventing a start today.

Two fear triggers: the absence of hands-on form correction with a surgical and back-pain history, and 'I guess I'll probably be starting something new, which is exciting, but a little scary.' He handled the first transparently and well by naming it as the con and reframing on support volume, and answered the second with one line ('That's how it's supposed to feel. That's a good thing'). None of the scripted moves ran — no certainty question, no pleasure/pain framing, no bridge, plane or burned-before analogy.

Script gap: there is no play for 'is this product even for people like me?'. The prospect raised, unprompted and politely, that the brand's site contains no female testimonial and never uses the words woman or female. The rep confirmed the premise ('90% of our audience is men... we push it more onto men') and answered with anecdote and then by showing her photographs of his girlfriend's body. A representation objection from a qualified female buyer has no scripted path, no proof asset and no case study to point at.

Clinical-fit trigger with no scripted play. Knee surgery, shoulder surgery, seven broken bones in the left foot and right ankle, and current episodic back pain under load that she manages by stopping mid-workout. The rep asked well, then closed the topic by minimising it — 'So you're fine on that front as well?' and 'I'm glad you're not like, well, I've got three herniated discs' — with no clearance question before selling a guaranteed 8 kg load progression.

notes: Much the strongest discovery in this batch — real baseline, a rephrased injury probe, a sharp diagnosis of nutrition as the bottleneck — attached to no consequence frame, no commitment check and no ask. This was a six-day-a-week trainer, already spending roughly $1,600 a month, who said 'this sounds good' and left without an agreement or an onboarding slot. The single coachable fix: after the 1-10 check, ask for the business.
